overview: Covers the current state of open spaces and urban greening in PCMC, ties in previous urban heat analysis, and recommends greening/heat-reduction measures. Discussed jointly since green cover directly affects heat mitigation.
current_situation: Per URDPFI norm, 10-12 sq.m. open space/person is required. PCMC currently has only 1.12 sq.m./person (gardens/playgrounds/recreational = 4% / 378 Ha of city area, based on 2025 population estimate of 33.84 lakh). Total DP area ~17,312 Ha (59% developed, 41% undeveloped). Recreational land ~2% of total city area, concentrated in the city centre.
challenges: Gap between demand and availability of green spaces (need ~11.8 sq. km citywide per URDPFI)
Lack of landscape restoration approach; several gardens poorly maintained
Weak ward-level relationship data between vegetation and Urban Heat Island effect
No ward-level biodiversity registers (only city-level register exists)
Need to prioritise native-species plantation over generic greening
climate_risks: 50% of the city faces extreme heat (per Doc B)
existing_initiatives: PCMC Paryavaran Sanskar Udyan - biodiversity park with native vegetation
City-level biodiversity inventory prepared by PCMC
Major parks/recreational spaces incl. Bird Valley Park, Akurdi (list not exhaustive in source)

strategies.name: Establish a baseline for per-capita open/green space, raise to URDPFI standard of 10-12 sq.m./person by 2035.
Identify and verify heat hotspots, analyse contributing factors, take measures to reduce heat.
Map, plan and integrate Blue-Green Infrastructure (BGI) in a phase-wise manner.
Develop Sponge Streets & Green Mobility Corridors (Harit Setu Integration).
Restore, maintain and enhance the city's biodiversity and ecosystem.
Create a comprehensive capacity-building and awareness programme.
